decision: W1 tracer (branch worktree-agent-a60a98e31a294cc4a, 2ff3bae): a real frame is 1312 dispatches in 21.7 ms; weights per frame 5.94 GB (dense 2.88, experts 1.01, tower 2.06); the big GEMVs already stream at 346 to 378 GB/s, so 5.94 GB at 378 GB/s is a 15.7 ms floor and the 14.6 ms target is below it; 1020 dispatches under 20 us cost about 4.9 ms, serial-encoder idle about 2.7 ms, five narrow GEMV shapes below 250 GB/s cost 2.35 ms, rmsnorm 1.4 ms, sampling 0.77 ms
why: the tracer uses one pass per dispatch (Apple GPUs sample only at stage boundaries), so per-dispatch windows overstate by about 1.5 us; frame totals come from an untraced encoder
result: confirms: 30 percent needs fewer bytes; fusion and concurrency can win 3 to 5 ms

decision: W3 lossless bf16 (branch worktree-agent-a062a03fb9ea93b33, 6099d2e): mantissas are incompressible (6.97 of 7 bits), exponents carry 2.6 to 2.9 bits, floor 10.6 to 10.9 bits per weight; a per-weight 3-bit exponent code with a per-tile window and byte escapes reaches 11.3 bits per weight, 29 percent fewer bytes, exact round trip on 17 real matrices; the packed GEMV is bit-identical but unpack-bound at about 285 GB/s physical (400 logical), so it wins 12 to 17 percent only on K=2048 shapes with N of 4096 and up, ties on the N=2048 long-K shapes and loses on narrow ones; projected 1.28 ms per frame (6 percent) packing the nine winning families, 1.02 GB fewer bytes
why: the byte saving is real but the kernel has to become DRAM-bound (40 percent fewer unpack ops, or split-K) before the full 4 ms shows
result: candidate: integrate selectively, 1.3 ms; the rest of the 30 percent is not reachable losslessly on this evidence

decision: W2 GEMV (branch worktree-agent-a8c39d99cbfdfba0b, 66c3991): the stream ceiling measured 383 GB/s; the tuned kernel already runs the big shapes at 356 to 373 GB/s; a bit-identical prototype with 4 tiles in flight per lane (r1u4v2s1x2sg) lifts the narrow shapes (gdn a/b 28 to 47 GB/s, router 177 to 218) and a multi-matrix dispatch removes about 2.5 us per dispatch it folds; best per shape plus grouping projects 1.18 ms per frame; the kbench 0.379 ms reading was a first-call warm-up artifact (M=1 always runs the GEMV whatever tile is asked); the default schedule costs about 5 ms per frame so the tuner stays
why: event-chained round-robin timing was needed, since back-to-back buffers overlapped and sequential runs drifted 256 to 351 GB/s

decision: W4 MoE decode (branch worktree-agent-a5b435c51dd155f99, d39510b): expert width is 512 not 768; an integer FP8 decode in place of the 256-entry table lifts gate-up to 97 percent of the read ceiling and down to the 8 MB read time; the whole MoE layer as three dispatches (bf16 router+shared+gate pass, routing+routed gate-up, routed down+shared down+combine) takes 112 us against 167 for the shipped 12 dispatches, bit-identical on synthetic data with a parity test that fails on a reordered sum; projected 2.2 ms per frame; a one-threadgroup-per-expert fusion was a dead end (8 threadgroups on 40 cores) and a spin-wait kernel hung the GPU for 12 minutes and was deleted; lossless FP8 compression tops out at 7.3 bits per weight (9 percent) so no prototype
why: bit-identical and the largest single candidate so far

decision: W6 tower (branch worktree-agent-a6bcf433fff35e8b6, d3ed451): the real tower step at position 500 is 6.8 ms without samplers, 7.6 with; GEMVs stream 2.06 GB at 354 GB/s, so a 5.6 ms floor; no gaps (chain equals the sum of groups); bit-identical fusions (q/k norm+rope+kv in one dispatch, embed+concat norms, w1+w3+silu, attention split 8 with in-order combine, gate and residual folds) take the chain from 6.79 to 6.25 ms, faster in 7 of 7 rounds; dumps byte-identical, compare.py passes; a GQA key-sharing variant was slower
why: small but clean; the tower is at the DRAM floor

decision: W6 saw sample_tower go from 0.07 ms to 1.3 to 1.8 ms per call after about 20:00 on both schedules, other kernels unaffected; its unconfirmed hypothesis is that the samplers one 1024-thread threadgroup with 21 KB of threadgroup memory needs a free GPU core and loses it to other GPU clients
why: sampler time sits on the critical path 10 times per frame, so this inflates every with-sampler number taken since
result: open: confirm on a quiet GPU before trusting end-to-end numbers
